content_scripts.comment: Whatnot page-world script (MAIN world, document_start) so its WebSocket.prototype patch is installed BEFORE Whatnot's Phoenix client opens its live/commerce sockets. An async <script src> injection (content_script's fallback below) can lose that race: if the sockets are created first, attach() never runs for them, trackedSockets stays empty, and every start_auction send fails with 'No live or commerce socket available'. Same fix as eBay/Palmstreet/TikTok. content_script still injects injected.js as a guarded (__HL_LIVE_CONTROLS_INJECTED__) fallback for the readiness handshake.

eBay page-world script injected by the browser in the MAIN world at document_start, so its fetch/XHR patch is in place BEFORE eBay's app bundle captures a fetch reference (an async <script src> injection loses that race and misses the page's own GraphQL headers). content_script also injects it as a guarded fallback for the readiness handshake.

Palmstreet page-world script (MAIN world, document_start) so its fetch/XHR + WebSocket patch beats the page's Socket.IO + api bundle — the same race eBay solves. It sniffs the Firebase bearer off the page's own api.plantstory.app requests and taps the Socket.IO checkout frames. content_script also injects it as a guarded fallback for the readiness handshake.

TikTok page-world script (MAIN world, document_start) so its fetch/XHR patch is installed BEFORE TikTok's request-signing SDK loads — that ordering makes TikTok's signer wrap ours, so our same-origin start_auction call gets signed (msToken/X-Bogus/X-Gnarly) automatically (see injected-tiktok.ts SIGNING note). It also sniffs room_id/session_id off the seller's own streamer_desktop traffic and taps the auction queue + sold responses. content_script also injects it as a guarded fallback for the readiness handshake.
